name: Archelaus
overview: Archelaus was a male member of the tribe of Edom and is known as the son of Herod, according to Matthew 2:22. He was king of Judea and was born around 21 B.C. His mother was Malthace, a Samaritan. Archelaus is noted primarily for his royal position and lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Archelaus appears once in Scripture in Matthew 2:22. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided, so it is simply recognized as his proper name without additional significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Archelaus as the son of Herod, as indicated in Matthew 2:22. Beyond this, no further family relationships are explicitly mentioned in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Archelaus holds significance in the biblical narrative as a son of Herod who inherited the kingship over Judea. His identity links him to the Herodian dynasty during the time surrounding the early life of Jesus. This connection situates him within the historical and political context of the New Testament era.
